messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: multiple Private VPN tunnels to customer 'AcmeCorp' reporting asymmetric routing and packet drops; alert triggered by healthcheck: vpn-uc-eu/uc-eu-aws. Affected: egress to eu-central region from eu-west. Pager sent to on-call.
alyssa (on-call): I'm on it — taking pager. Trying to pull the latest tunnel/route metrics now.
mike (netops): I see BGP flaps on our side for ACME-prod-prefixes. Could be path-preference oscillation between DX1 and VPN1. Looking at RIB.
deepa (sre): Any customer-visible errors? Support ticket 8342 shows 503s for API requests originating from eu-central. Jordan, are customers actively impacted?
jordan (acct): Confirmed from account: several customers in EU seeing intermittent failures and slow retries. They flagged an ingest pipeline backpressure. Customer priority: high.
alyssa (on-call): Initial checks:
```
# show bgp summary vpn1
Neighbor 10.0.255.1    AS 64512  Up 00:23  prefixes 42  state Active
# show route acme-prefix
uc-eu: best via 10.0.255.1   weight 0  AS-path 64512  localpref 100
```
But route is flapping to alternate via dx1 with different AS path then back.
mike (netops): Running traceroute from GW to customer edge:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max
 1  10.10.0.1 (10.10.0.1)  0.36 ms  0.32 ms  0.29 ms
 2  198.51.100.1 (198.51.100.1)  5.12 ms  4.98 ms *
 3  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  12.44 ms  12.31 ms  12.27 ms
```
Seeing some packet loss on hop 2 intermittently.
priya (on-call-shadow): Could be a vendor (cloud provider) ECMP imbalance combined with our BGP attribute differences. Recommend prepending on the preferred path to force sticky selection while we investigate.
alyssa (on-call): Agreed. Plan: 1) Apply localpref/prepend to bias to dx1 for acme prefixes 2) Engage cloud support 3) Monitor healthchecks and customer errors. Anyone object?
deepa (sre): Do it. Also enable additional logging for token-level throttles so we can correlate errors.
engops-bot: runbook step executed: applied route-map ACME-PREFER-DX1 to peering vrf 'acme-prod'. (cmd: apply route-map ACME-PREFER-DX1 out on bgp vrf)
mike (netops): Applied prepend of +3 on VPN1 path; removing one of the 2-as hops from advertisement on dx1 to normalize AS-paths. Will watch BGP.
alyssa (on-call): Cloud support ticket opened: CS-9921 — asked for interface counters and their ECMP bucket distribution for the last 15m. They replied they see microbursts on provider fabric for eu-west-2 and are investigating.
support-lead: Please prepare customer-facing blurb: "We're seeing intermittent connectivity degradation between eu-west and eu-central for some Private VPN connections. We're actively mitigating; no data loss expected." Jordan please send.
jordan (acct): Drafted and sent to customer 03:45 UTC. They acknowledged and asked for ETA.
mike (netops): BGP stabilized after route-map. RIB shows consistent next-hop now.
```
# show bgp neighbors 10.0.255.1
Status: Established, prefixes 42, packets in/out stable
```
deepa (sre): Application errors have dropped to baseline for 10m. Dashboard latency back to normal.
alyssa (on-call): Moving to monitoring mode. I'll leave the route-map in place for 2 hours and then test removal to ensure provider fabric is stable. Priya, can you monitor incidents channel and escalate if error rate creeps back up?
priya (on-call-shadow): Watching, will ping at +15m and +60m or earlier if symptom returns.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 55m. Alyssa currently assigned; handoff to Priya if no further action.
engops-bot: Timeline update: incident detected 03:41 UTC; mitigation applied 03:48 UTC; partial mitigation confirmed 03:56 UTC.
alyssa (on-call): Quick postmortem notes:
- Trigger: BGP path oscillation between DX and VPN due to cloud ECMP microbursts causing asymmetry
- Immediate mitigation: route-map/AS-prepend to prefer DX path for affected prefixes
- Next steps: coordinate with cloud provider to root cause their ECMP imbalance, schedule permanent route-policy to avoid churn, and run controlled removal tomorrow during low traffic
support-lead: Thanks — I'll post an internal incident summary and tag infra/network for follow-up. Marking P1->P2 after stabilization. :white_check_mark:
mike (netops): Filed internal follow-up ticket INFRA-1284 to add automated detection for this flapping pattern.
alyssa (on-call): Closing thread for now; will update if anything changes. :wave:
